name: Splitting and extracting PDF pages
title: How to split a PDF and extract exactly the pages you need
metaTitle: How to Split a PDF Free (Pages and Ranges)
metaDescription: Split a PDF into single pages or custom ranges, extract only the pages you need, delete the rest, and cut a big file down to fit an email attachment limit.
intro: Splitting, extracting and deleting are three names for the same underlying edit: deciding which pages end up in which file. The difference is what you keep. Splitting produces several files, extracting produces one file holding a subset, and deleting produces the original minus a few pages. These guides cover the range syntax every tool uses, the every-N-pages mode, and the specific case that sends most people looking in the first place, a PDF too large to email.
answer: Open the PDF in a split tool and choose a mode: single pages, custom ranges such as 1-3,5,8-, or every N pages. Extracting keeps the chosen pages in one new file; splitting produces several files. The original on your disk is never modified by any of them.

posts.title: How to split a PDF into separate pages or ranges
posts.metaTitle: How to Split a PDF Into Pages or Ranges
posts.metaDescription: Split a PDF into single pages, custom ranges like 1-3,5,8- or fixed chunks of every N pages. The range syntax explained, plus how the output files are named.
secondaryKeywords: divide a pdf into multiple files
posts.answer: Open the PDF in a split tool, choose a mode, and download the results. Three modes cover almost everything: split into single pages, split by custom ranges such as 1-3,5,8-, or split every N pages into equal chunks. Output arrives as separate PDFs or one ZIP archive.

body.x: Splitting is the cheapest edit you can make to a PDF. No page is re-rendered; the tool copies the page objects you asked for into new documents and rebuilds each page tree. Text stays selectable, vectors stay sharp, and images are byte-identical to the originals.
The three modes, and when each is right

Output
Use it for

One file per range you type

You want a subset, not a set of files

body.x: Splitting step by step

items.x: Go to [split PDF](/tools/split-pdf) and drop the file in. It is read in your browser, so a 300 MB file is no slower to load than it is to open in a reader.
Single pages, custom ranges, or every N pages. If you are not sure, start with custom ranges: it covers the other two.
Use the syntax below. The preview should show the page count for each output before you commit.
Most tools use the source filename plus a suffix. Setting a prefix such as `Contract_` up front saves renaming a dozen files afterwards.
One or two files download individually. More than that usually arrives as a single ZIP.

body.x: Split a PDF by pages or ranges without uploading it to a server.
The range syntax
Almost every PDF tool, from Acrobat to command-line utilities to browser tools, accepts the same notation. Pages are 1-indexed, meaning the first page is 1, not 0.

body.caption: Range notation, using a 20-page document as the example.
head: You type
You get
Notes
rows: A single page is a valid range
Commas separate ranges; each becomes its own file
Five one-page files, or one file of odd pages
Depends on whether the tool is splitting or extracting
Some tools accept a descending range; many reject it

body.x: Watch out for documents whose printed page numbers do not match their physical ones. A report with a cover, a blank verso and roman-numbered front matter can have "page 1" printed on physical page 7. Range syntax always means the physical position, so count thumbnails, not the numbers on the paper.
Every N pages, with a real example

A 240-page manual made of twelve chapters, each exactly 20 pages, splits into chapters with a single instruction: every 20 pages. You get 12 files without typing 12 ranges. The mode is only useful when the unit really is fixed, so check two boundaries before you trust it: does file 2 start at the top of chapter 2, and does the last file end where the document does? If chapter 4 runs to 21 pages, every subsequent boundary is wrong.

The other genuinely useful case is size-limited splitting: a 90 MB scan divided into six 15-page parts so each attachment stays under a mail server ceiling. See [splitting a large PDF for email](/blog/split/split-large-pdf-for-email) for the arithmetic.
Splitting at bookmarks

If the PDF has a proper outline, splitting at top-level bookmarks is far better than counting pages, because the boundaries follow the document's own structure and survive a revision that changes the page count. Not every tool offers it, and it only works when the file actually has bookmarks: a scanned document or a PDF printed from a web page will have none at all.
Why the parts add up to more than the whole

Split a 10 MB PDF into ten files and the total is often 12 to 14 MB. This is expected, not a bug. Fonts, colour profiles and any image used on more than one page are shared resources in the original, stored once. When pages are separated, each output needs its own copy of everything its pages reference. A document with a logo on every page and two embedded font families will duplicate all of it into every part.
If total size matters, compress after splitting rather than before. Compression can also de-duplicate identical objects within each part.
Shrink the split files before you send or archive them.
Other ways to split

items: **macOS Preview**, show thumbnails with ⌥⌘2, select the pages you want and drag them onto the Desktop. macOS creates a new PDF from the selection. Fine for one extraction, tedious for twelve.
**Print to PDF with a page range**, works everywhere, but re-renders the document. Links, bookmarks and form fields are lost, and the output can be larger than the input.
**Adobe Acrobat**, Organize Pages → Split, with by-page-count, by-file-size and by-bookmark options. The by-file-size mode is genuinely handy and rare elsewhere.
**qpdf**, free, offline, scriptable, and the most structurally faithful of the lot.

body.x:
# Pages 1-3 into their own file
qpdf input.pdf --pages input.pdf 1-3 -- part1.pdf

# Every page as its own file: out-01.pdf, out-02.pdf, ...
qpdf --split-pages input.pdf out.pdf

# Chunks of 20 pages each
qpdf --split-pages=20 manual.pdf chapter.pdf
What splitting does not do

It does not remove anything hidden. Content covered by a black rectangle, cropped out of view, or sitting in a layer that is switched off travels with the page into the new file. If you are splitting a document to share only part of it with someone, the pages you keep are still carrying everything they carried before. [Flatten](/tools/flatten-pdf) the output and [remove the metadata](/tools/remove-metadata) before sending.
It also does not fix a broken file. A PDF that fails to split usually fails to open properly too. Run it through [repair](/tools/repair-pdf) first, then split the repaired copy.

faqs.q: How do I split a PDF into individual pages?
faqs.a: Open the file in a split tool and choose the single pages mode. A 40-page document becomes 40 one-page PDFs, normally delivered as a single ZIP so you are not accepting 40 separate downloads.

faqs.q: What does the range 1-3,5,8- mean?
faqs.a: Three ranges separated by commas: pages 1 to 3, page 5 on its own, and pages 8 to the end of the document. In split mode each range becomes its own file; in extract mode all of them land in one new PDF.

faqs.q: Does splitting a PDF reduce the quality?
faqs.a: No. Pages are copied as objects rather than re-rendered, so text, vectors and images are identical to the source. Quality only changes if you compress the parts afterwards.

faqs.q: Can I split a PDF on a Mac without extra software?
faqs.a: Yes. Open it in Preview, press Option+Command+2 for thumbnails, select the pages you want and drag them to the Desktop. macOS creates a new PDF from the selection. It works well once and gets tedious quickly.

faqs.q: Why are my split files bigger in total than the original?
faqs.a: Fonts, colour profiles and repeated images are stored once in the original but must be copied into each output file. A document with a logo on every page and two embedded fonts will duplicate all of that into every part.

posts.title: How to extract specific pages from a PDF
posts.metaTitle: How to Extract Pages From a PDF
posts.metaDescription: Extract pages from a PDF free: select thumbnails or enter a page range, save the pages you need in a new PDF, and leave the original unchanged.

pull pages out of a pdf

posts.answer: Extract pages from a PDF free in your browser: select the thumbnails you want or enter a range such as 4-9, then download a new PDF containing only those pages. The source file is unchanged. Extraction keeps your chosen subset in one file, unlike splitting, which creates multiple files.

body.x: The three page operations get confused constantly, and choosing the wrong one is why people end up with 47 files they did not want. The distinction is simply what you are left holding.

body.caption: Extract, split and delete, applied to a 50-page report.
head: Operation
You specify
You get
Original
rows: Several PDFs covering the whole document

body.x: Extracting, step by step

items.x: Go to [extract pages](/tools/extract-pages) and drop the PDF in. Every page appears as a numbered thumbnail.
Click thumbnails to toggle them, or type a range such as `4-9` or `2,7,15-18`. Selections do not have to be contiguous.
Choose **one combined file** to keep the pages together in order, or **one file per page** if each page is going to a different place.
Extraction keeps the original document order regardless of the order you clicked. If you need a different sequence, extract first and then [reorder](/tools/organize-pdf).
The new file contains only the pages you chose. Nothing was written back to the source.

body.x: Pull out exactly the pages you need and keep the rest of the document intact.
Things people actually extract

items: **The signature page** of a long contract, to send back on its own instead of returning 60 pages.
**One chapter** of a textbook or manual for a class, a meeting or a printout.
**A single invoice** from a monthly statement batch that arrived as one file.
**The results section** of a report, when the reviewer asked for the findings and not the methodology.
**One certificate** from a batch generated for a whole cohort.
**The two pages that matter** from a 120-page terms document, to quote in an email.

body.x: The print-to-PDF shortcut, and its cost

You can extract pages anywhere without a dedicated tool: open the PDF in any viewer, press **Ctrl+P**, type the page range, and choose **Save as PDF** as the destination. It works on every platform with no software at all.
The cost is that this re-renders the document rather than copying it. Compare the two routes before you use it for anything that matters.

head: Extract tool
Print to PDF with a range
rows: Yes, if they point into the kept range
Rescaled to the selected paper size
Often larger than the extracted portion

body.x: Print-to-PDF is a perfectly good way to pull one page out of a manual for a colleague. It is a bad way to extract a page from a fillable form, an accessible document, or anything with a table of contents you want to keep working.
macOS Preview and command line
On a Mac, show thumbnails with **⌥⌘2**, ⌘-click the pages you want, and drag the selection onto the Desktop. macOS builds a new PDF from it. For repeatable work, qpdf is exact and scriptable:

# Pages 4-9 into a new file
qpdf report.pdf --pages report.pdf 4-9 -- section.pdf

# Non-contiguous: pages 2, 7 and 15-18
qpdf report.pdf --pages report.pdf 2,7,15-18 -- selected.pdf

# Pull the same page range out of every PDF in a folder
for f in *.pdf; do qpdf "$f" --pages "$f" 1 -- "covers/$f"; done

Extracting a page does **not** remove anything hidden on it. Text under a black box, content outside the crop box, comments, and hidden layers all travel into the new file. If the point of extracting was to share less, [flatten](/tools/flatten-pdf) the result and [strip its metadata](/blog/privacy/remove-metadata-from-pdf) before sending it.
What comes with the pages

An extracted file inherits the source document's metadata: title, author, producer, and the creation date of the original rather than of your extraction. If you extracted a single page from a colleague's report, their name is now in your file's author field. Check it with [edit metadata](/tools/edit-metadata), which takes about ten seconds.

Bookmarks pointing at pages you did not keep are dropped or left dangling depending on the tool, and printed page numbers do not renumber, so an extracted range that starts at physical page 12 will still say 12 on the first sheet. If that is confusing for the reader, re-apply [page numbers](/tools/page-numbers) to the extract.
Extract, or delete the rest?

They reach the same place from opposite ends, so pick whichever needs less typing. Keeping 6 pages out of 50: extract. Removing 6 pages from 50: [delete those pages](/blog/split/delete-pages-from-pdf). The rule of thumb is to specify the smaller set, because every page you type is a page you can get wrong.

faqs.q: How do I save just one page of a PDF?
faqs.a: Open the file in an extract tool, select that single page and download. Alternatively press Ctrl+P, enter the page number in the range box and choose Save as PDF, though that route drops links, bookmarks and form fields.

faqs.q: What is the difference between extracting and splitting a PDF?
faqs.a: Extracting produces one new file containing the pages you chose. Splitting divides the whole document into several files. Extract when you want a subset; split when you need the entire document broken into parts.

faqs.q: Does extracting pages change the original PDF?
faqs.a: No. Extraction reads the source and writes a new file. The original stays on your disk exactly as it was, which is why it is safe to experiment with the range until the output looks right.

faqs.q: Can I extract pages that are not next to each other?
faqs.a: Yes. Type a list such as 2,7,15-18, or click individual thumbnails. The extracted file keeps them in document order, not in the order you selected them.

faqs.q: Do extracted pages keep their form fields?
faqs.a: A proper extract tool preserves fillable fields and their values. Extracting by printing to PDF does not, because printing flattens the form into static page content.

posts.title: How to delete pages from a PDF
posts.metaTitle: How to Delete Pages From a PDF
posts.metaDescription: Remove blank pages, cover sheets, ad pages or a whole appendix from a PDF. Delete by thumbnail or page range in your browser, then download the clean file.
secondaryKeywords: remove a page from a pdf mac
posts.answer: Open the PDF in a page editor, select the thumbnails of the pages you want gone or type a range such as 2,5,11-13, then delete and download. Deleting pages from a copy is safe: the original file on your disk is unchanged until you replace it yourself.

body.x: Most PDFs arrive with pages nobody wants. A fax cover sheet, a blank verso from a duplex scan, two pages of advertising bound into a magazine article, a 30-page terms appendix on a 4-page invoice. Removing them makes the file smaller, cheaper to print and quicker to read.

body.caption: What people delete, and how to find it.
head: Unwanted pages
Where they come from
How to spot them
rows: Every even page, and they are the smallest pages in the file
Page 1, and sometimes the last page
Full-bleed colour pages between article pages
A long uniform block at the end
A double feed in the scanner
Two adjacent thumbnails that look identical

body.x: Deleting pages

items.x: Go to [delete pages](/tools/delete-pages) and drop the PDF in. Thumbnails appear with their page numbers.
Click the pages to mark them for removal, or type a range such as `2,5,11-13`. Shift-click selects a run; Ctrl-click (⌘-click on macOS) adds scattered pages.
The tool should show the resulting page count. Removing 6 pages from a 48-page file must leave 42. If it does not, your selection is not what you think it is.
A new file is written. Your original is untouched on disk.
Open the result and look at the pages either side of each deletion. That is where a mis-selected page shows up immediately.

body.x: Remove pages from a PDF in your browser, with no upload and no account.
Finding the blank pages

Scanned blank pages are almost never blank. Dust on the platen, show-through from the printed side, and paper texture all leave marks, so an automatic "remove blank pages" filter that tests for pure white will skip most of them. Two better approaches:

items: **Sort by page weight.** A scanned page with text on it might be 180 KB; an empty one is nearer 15 KB. Any tool that shows per-page size makes the blanks obvious.

**Use the pattern.** A single-sided original scanned in duplex produces blanks at every even page. Select 2, 4, 6, 8 with a range like `2-48` and a step, or simply Ctrl-click the even thumbnails; the regularity makes this quick.

body.x: Before deleting anything from a scan, confirm the blanks really are blank. A faint handwritten note or a rubber stamp on the reverse of one page is exactly the thing an automatic filter throws away.
Other ways to do it

head: Platform
Method
Notes
rows: Preview → ⌥⌘2 for thumbnails → select → Delete key
Then File → Export as PDF for a clean copy
Edge can view and annotate but not delete pages
A page editor that runs locally
Works identically on Windows, Linux and ChromeOS
Also has a Delete Blank Pages action
Note the inversion: you list what to keep

body.x: The qpdf idiom is worth internalising because it is the same idea as extracting: rather than naming the pages to remove, you name everything else. `1-4,7-z` keeps pages 1 through 4 and 7 through the end, which deletes pages 5 and 6. The letter `z` means the last page.
What breaks when a page disappears

items: **Bookmarks pointing at deleted pages** become dead entries that jump nowhere, or vanish, depending on the tool.
**Internal links** from a table of contents behave the same way.

**Printed page numbers do not renumber.** The number is drawn into the page content. After deleting page 12, page 13 still says 13. Strip and re-apply them with [page numbers](/tools/page-numbers) if it matters.
**Digital signatures are invalidated**, because the signed byte range no longer exists.
**Total page counts in the text go stale.** "Page 3 of 48" printed in a footer is just text.

body.x: Deleting a page is not redacting it

This one matters. PDF supports **incremental updates**: an editor can append changes to the end of a file rather than rewriting it, which is fast and preserves the ability to undo. The consequence is that a "deleted" page can still exist as an orphaned object inside the file, invisible in every viewer but recoverable with a text editor or a forensic tool.

If the pages you removed were confidential, that is not good enough. Use a tool that fully rewrites the document rather than appending an update, then [flatten](/tools/flatten-pdf) it and [remove the metadata](/tools/remove-metadata), which can otherwise retain the original page count and modification history.

The same applies to content you covered with a black rectangle. Drawing a box over text hides it visually and leaves the text underneath fully selectable. Deleting the page removes it properly; covering it does not.
Strip author names, timestamps and edit history before you send a trimmed document.
Delete, or keep what you want?

If you are removing more than about half the document, [extracting the pages you want](/blog/split/extract-pages-from-pdf) is faster and less error-prone: fewer numbers to type means fewer numbers to get wrong. And if the reason you are deleting pages is file size, deleting rarely helps as much as [compression](/tools/compress-pdf), because the weight is usually in the images on the pages you are keeping.

faqs.q: How do I delete a page from a PDF for free?
faqs.a: Open the file in a browser-based page editor, click the thumbnail of the page you want removed, and download the result. On a Mac you can also use Preview: show thumbnails with Option+Command+2, select the page and press Delete.

faqs.q: Can I delete PDF pages in Windows without installing anything?
faqs.a: Not with a built-in Windows feature. Edge displays and annotates PDFs but cannot remove pages, and there is no page editor in File Explorer. A browser-based tool is the closest equivalent.

faqs.q: How do I remove all the blank pages from a scan?
faqs.a: Blank scanned pages usually carry speckles, so filters looking for pure white miss them. Sort by page size, since an empty page is a fraction of the weight of one with text, or select every even page if the blanks came from duplex-scanning a single-sided original.

faqs.q: Does deleting a page make the PDF smaller?
faqs.a: Only if the page contained something substantial. Removing a text page from a 30 MB scanned document changes almost nothing; removing a full-page photograph can save several megabytes. Compression usually achieves far more.

faqs.q: Is a deleted page really gone from the file?
faqs.a: Not always. PDFs can be saved as incremental updates that append changes rather than rewriting the file, leaving orphaned objects behind. For confidential pages, use a tool that fully rewrites the document, then flatten it and strip the metadata.

posts.title: How to split PDFs for an email attachment limit
posts.metaTitle: Split PDFs for Email Attachment Limits
posts.metaDescription: Compare compression, chapter-based splitting and sharing links when a PDF is too large to email. Learn how message encoding affects attachment size.
posts.primaryKeyword: split PDF for email attachment limit
posts.answer: To fit a PDF under an email attachment limit, check the exact limit, split the file into logical page ranges, and leave headroom for email encoding. PrintxPDF lets you create ordered PDF parts in your browser without signup or a watermark, while preserving the original file.

body.x: Your provider and the recipient's provider can enforce different limits. The lower one applies, and work or school accounts may have administrator-set rules. Check the current help page and leave room for the message itself.
The limits, and the hidden third

body.caption: Published sending limits checked October 2026. Business and school accounts may have custom policies.
head: Service
Sending limit
What happens above it
rows: Gmail may replace oversize attachments with a Google Drive link
Use OneDrive or another approved sharing service
Check with the administrator or use an approved file-sharing link
Use a file-sharing link if the recipient can access it
20 MB; up to 5 GB with Mail Drop
Mail Drop links are available for up to 30 days
Share using Proton Drive or another service
Varies by administrator and recipient system
Check both organizations' rules before sending

body.x: Email encoding can add roughly one-third to an attachment's transmitted size, but providers do not all describe or enforce limits the same way. Leave room for the message and check the sender's interface and the recipient's rules instead of treating one file-size target as universal.
There is no safe file-size target that applies to every provider. Use the limit for the sender's account, leave room for message overhead, and ask the recipient if their system has a lower cap.
Compress first. Almost always.

Splitting is a workaround; [compression](/tools/compress-pdf) is a fix. The recipient gets one attachment instead of four, nobody has to reassemble anything, and the document stays whole. Try it first and only split if compression is not enough.
The PrintxPDF compressor has three presets, not a custom DPI or grayscale control. The result depends on the source PDF:

Documents where search, copy and sharp text matter
Turns pages into images; may reduce a scan, but text is no longer selectable

Deciding what to do

body.caption: Pick the route that matches the file and the recipient.
head: Situation
Do this
rows: Try Light first; compare Medium or Strong on a copy if searchable text is not required. Check the output size.
Already-compressed PDF that exceeds the confirmed cap
Split it into parts sized for the sender and recipient limits, leaving room for the message.
Do not email it. Share a cloud link.
Legal or signed document that must not change
Split, never compress. Compression re-encodes and breaks signatures.
Recipient uses a company or school email system
Ask for its limit or use an approved sharing link.
You do not know the recipient's limit
Ask the recipient or choose a suitably conservative size; no one target fits all systems.
Compress hard, or share a link, and say why.

body.x: Splitting it properly

items.x: Choose a per-message target below the confirmed limit, allowing room for message overhead. Divide the file size by that target and round up to estimate the number of parts.
Divide the page count by the number of parts. A 68 MB, 240-page file split into 5 gives 48 pages per part. Use the every-N-pages mode with N = 48.

Nudge the boundaries so parts break between chapters or sections rather than mid-sentence. Custom ranges are worth the extra typing here. See [splitting into pages or ranges](/blog/split/split-pdf-into-pages).
Sizes are rarely even, because pages are not equally heavy. One 90-page part of thin text can be smaller than a 20-page part of scans. Verify each file individually against your target.
Use `Report_2026_part1of4.pdf` rather than `Report (1).pdf`. The person on the other end has to work out the order without you.

items.h: Send in order, one per message
items.x: Say in the first message how many parts there are, and mention how to reassemble them if the recipient needs the whole document.

body.x: Split by page count or by custom ranges, with the page count for each part shown before you commit.

Never split a PDF into parts and then compress each part separately if the document is being submitted somewhere official. Page numbering, signatures and any certification will not survive, and a reviewer receiving four unrelated-looking files is a good way to have a submission rejected.
The option most people should take instead
Splitting a document across four emails is a bad experience for whoever receives it. A link is better in almost every case where it is allowed:

items: **Google Drive**, Gmail can replace attachments over its limit with a Drive link. Check the sharing permission before sending.
**OneDrive**, Outlook offers the same thing, and Microsoft 365 accounts include 1 TB.
**iCloud Mail Drop**, up to 5 GB, built into Apple Mail, links expire after 30 days.
Other file-sharing services may work too; check their current size, expiry and access rules.
For anything confidential, check whether your organisation permits these services before using one. Many do not.

body.x: Why the PDF is large in the first place

Worth knowing, because it changes what you should do. A 50 MB PDF is almost always one of three things: a scanned document stored at 300 or 600 DPI, a set of pages carrying full-resolution photographs, or an export from design software that embedded every asset at print resolution. All three [compress dramatically](/blog/compress/how-to-compress-a-pdf). A 50 MB PDF that is genuinely mostly text is rare, and usually means the file has accumulated revision history through incremental saves, which a full rewrite clears out.

If the file came from a scanner, also run [OCR](/tools/ocr-pdf) while you are at it. It adds a small amount of size and makes the document searchable, which is what the recipient will want next anyway.

faqs.q: What is the maximum attachment size for Gmail?
faqs.a: Personal Gmail allows up to 25 MB in total attachments. Gmail can replace oversize attachments with a Google Drive link. Work and school accounts may have administrator-set limits, and the recipient's system may be lower.

faqs.q: What is the Outlook attachment size limit?
faqs.a: Microsoft publishes a 20 MB email-size limit for Outlook.com. Microsoft 365 and Exchange limits can depend on organization settings, so check with the administrator or use an approved sharing link.

faqs.q: Should I compress or split a large PDF?
faqs.a: Try Light compression if you need text to stay searchable and selectable. Medium and Strong turn pages into images, with size reduction depending on the source. Split or use a sharing link if you cannot accept that trade-off. Preserve signed originals because rewriting can invalidate signatures.

faqs.q: How do I split a PDF into equal parts by file size?
faqs.a: Divide the total size by your per-message target to get the number of parts, then divide the page count by that number and split every N pages. Check each part afterwards, because pages vary in weight and the split will not be perfectly even.

faqs.q: Why does my 24 MB PDF bounce from a 25 MB limit?
faqs.a: Encoding can increase the transmitted size, and some limits include the message body or are set by the recipient's organization. Check both systems rather than relying on one universal file-size calculation.

body.x: Use the right page range before you split

Page labels printed on a document do not always match the PDF viewer’s page count. A cover sheet, blank page, or appendix can make printed page 1 appear as PDF page 2. Check thumbnails before entering a range. If the document is a scan, look for a page number in the image rather than relying only on the viewer counter.
Keep private information out of the wrong output
